# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: with no failing val trace and val already at 1.000, I treated the objective as held-out generalization and shipped a batch of SAFE deterministic guards (tools) + explicit operating-guide prose (policy) targeting the airline domain's known un-enforced policy rules. Can't cite a LEDGER row yet (first iteration).
- Key design principle used: guards RAISE on genuine violations only, never auto-correct — so a policy-compliant call is byte-identical to the seed and no passing task can regress. This is the right posture when you cannot see failing traces and the gate punishes any regression.
- Plateau/stall signal: structural — the gate compares against val=1.000 on ONE task, so val cannot go up; a single-task val split gives the hill-climber no gradient. The real signal for this capability would be a larger/held-out airline split.
- What to try next iteration: if real failing traces appear, prioritize clusters D (cancel eligibility) and E (compensation) with semi-deterministic guards (enforce the objective legs in code, leave judgment legs to prose). Otherwise measure prose length vs. value and prune.
